mainTopic: Conduct and צניעות in the בית הכסא: learning from one's רבי, the left hand, protection from מזיקין, privacy distances, and true modesty.
overview: The amud is all about proper conduct in the בית הכסא. It opens with ברייתות in which רבי עקיבא and then בן עזאי followed their teachers into the bathroom to learn their practices. In each story the student defends himself with the same words: 'תורה היא וללמוד אני צריך'. רב כהנא uses the same words after hiding under רב's bed. The גמרא then gives several reasons, from אמוראים and תנאים, why one wipes with the left hand and not the right. Next come teachings and stories about how צניעות and silence protect a person from מזיקין in the bathroom, including the stories of אביי's lamb and רבא's wife. עולא and איסי בר נתן disagree about how far one must go for privacy, and the גמרא defends איסי בר נתן against sources from the laws of טהרות. A story about a eulogizer teaches that real צניעות is private behavior, and that false praise of the dead is punished. The amud ends with בן עזאי's advice to go early or late so as not to go far, and a protective formula against כשפים for someone who sat before preparing.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא learns three bathroom practices from רבי יהושע
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא reports that רבי עקיבא followed his teacher רבי יהושע into the bathroom and learned three practices from him.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבי עקיבא said: Once I went into the bathroom after רבי יהושע, and I learned three things from him. I learned that one does not relieve himself facing east and west, but north and south. I learned that one does not uncover himself standing, but sitting. And I learned that one does not wipe with the right hand, but with the left.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא in which רבי עקיבא reports three practices he learned by watching רבי יהושע in the bathroom.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These are three separate rules: which direction to face, when to uncover oneself (only once seated, for צניעות), and which hand to wipe with. All three were learned from the teacher's actions, not from his words. This is a classic case of שימוש תלמידי חכמים, learning from how a חכם behaves.

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Akiva said:
Once I entered
after Rabbi Yehoshua into the bathroom,
and I learned three things from him:
I learned that one does not relieve himself facing east and west
but rather north and south;
and I learned that one does not uncover himself standing
but sitting;
and I learned that one does not wipe with the right hand
but with the left.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens this passage with a ברייתא about bathroom conduct, continuing the broader discussion of modesty in the bathroom.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Face north–south, uncover only while seated, and wipe with the left hand.

steps.title: בן עזאי objects that this was disrespectful
steps.stepSummary: בן עזאי challenges רבי עקיבא: was it not brazen to watch your teacher so closely?
steps.simpleTranslation: בן עזאי said to him: You were so bold toward your teacher, to this extent?!
steps.whatsHappening: בן עזאי challenges רבי עקיבא's behavior. He is not challenging the three rules themselves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The objection is about כבוד הרב. Following your teacher into the bathroom and watching him seems to cross a line of respect. The challenge sets up רבי עקיבא's answer.

phrases.english: Ben Azzai said to him:
Were you bold toward your teacher to this extent?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the method of learning described in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי עקיבא's following his teacher into the bathroom
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Watching a רבי in such a private setting looks like a lack of respect.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא answers: it is תורה
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא answers that this is Torah, and he needs to learn it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: It is Torah, and I need to learn.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא defends himself: even bathroom conduct is part of Torah, so he had to learn it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer widens what counts as 'Torah' to include the most private personal conduct. The need to learn outweighs the apparent disrespect.

phrases.english: He said to him: It is Torah,
and I need to learn.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers בן עזאי's objection.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefinition of the value at stake
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Watching one's teacher in the bathroom is simply disrespect.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is a legitimate form of learning Torah.

steps.title: בן עזאי learns the same three practices from רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: A second ברייתא: בן עזאי followed רבי עקיבא and learned the same three practices.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: בן עזאי says: Once I went into the bathroom after רבי עקיבא, and I learned three things from him. I learned that one does not relieve himself facing east and west, but north and south. I learned that one does not uncover himself standing, but sitting. And I learned that one does not wipe with the right hand, but with the left.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a parallel ברייתא. This time the student, בן עזאי, does to רבי עקיבא exactly what רבי עקיבא did to his own teacher.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The text is truly repeated in the source, and it adds something new. It shows a chain of tradition: the same practice passed from רבי יהושע to רבי עקיבא to בן עזאי. The very person who objected now follows the same path.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think this is the same ברייתא copied twice. In the first, בן עזאי is the one objecting. Here he is the student doing the watching.

phrases.english: It was taught: Ben Azzai says:
Once I entered
after Rabbi Akiva into the bathroom,
and I learned three things from him:
I learned that one does not relieve himself facing east and west
but rather north and south;
and I learned that one does not uncover himself standing
but sitting;
and I learned that one does not wipe with the right hand
but with the left.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel ברייתא that shows the same practice continuing one generation later.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The same three practices, now passed from רבי עקיבא to בן עזאי.

steps.title: רבי יהודה raises the same objection
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה asks בן עזאי the same question about being brazen toward his teacher.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה said to him: You were so bold toward your teacher, to this extent?!
steps.whatsHappening: Now רבי יהודה objects to בן עזאי, just as בן עזאי had objected to רבי עקיבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The objection is the same: watching a רבי in the bathroom seems to violate כבוד הרב. The repetition sets up the same answer again.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda said to him:
Were you bold toward your teacher to this extent?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי יְהוּדָה: עַד כָּאן הֵעַזְתָּ פָּנֶיךָ בְּרַבְּךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges בן עזאי's behavior in step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: בן עזאי following רבי עקיבא into the bathroom
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It looks like a breach of respect for one's teacher.

steps.title: בן עזאי gives the same answer
steps.stepSummary: בן עזאי answers: it is Torah, and I need to learn.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: It is Torah, and I need to learn.
steps.whatsHappening: בן עזאי defends himself with the very words his teacher רבי עקיבא used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same answer is passed down along with the practices. The principle holds across generations: personal conduct is Torah and must be learned.

phrases.english: He said to him: It is Torah,
and I need to learn.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי יהודה's objection.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefinition of the value at stake
steps.terutzHavaAmina: This is disrespect to a teacher.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is the learning of Torah.

steps.title: רב כהנא hides under רב's bed
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא hid under רב's bed, heard רב with his wife, and remarked on how intense he was.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא went in and lay under רב's bed. He heard him chatting and laughing and taking care of his needs. He said to him: אבא's mouth is like someone who has never tasted a cooked dish.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a more extreme story in the same spirit. רב כהנא hid under his teacher רב's bed while רב was with his wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Taking care of his needs' is a polite way of referring to marital relations. רב כהנא's remark means רב acted as eagerly as a starving man. That seemed surprising to him from so great a חכם, which is why he spoke up and revealed he was there.

keyTerms.meaning: Took care of his needs (marital relations)
As if he never tasted a cooked dish

steps.confusionAlert: 'עשה צרכיו' here does not mean using the bathroom. In this context it refers to marital relations.

phrases.english: Rav Kahana went in,
and lay under Rav's bed.
He heard him chatting and laughing
and taking care of his needs.
He said to him: Abba's mouth is like
someone who has never tasted a cooked dish.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב כָּהֲנָא עָל, גְּנָא תּוּתֵיהּ פּוּרְיֵיהּ דְּרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third, more extreme example of a student watching a teacher in private.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A story showing a student observing his teacher's most private conduct.

steps.title: רב tells רב כהנא to leave
steps.stepSummary: רב is startled to find רב כהנא there and tells him to leave, because this is not proper conduct.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: כהנא, you are here? Leave, because this is not proper behavior.
steps.whatsHappening: רב himself objects, telling his student that being there is not דרך ארץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This time the objection comes from the teacher, not from a third party. It is also a stronger objection, because it concerns marital privacy. That raises the question of whether the principle still holds here.

phrases.english: He said to him: Kahana, you are here?
Leave, for this is not proper conduct.

steps.triggerLanguage: כָּהֲנָא, הָכָא אַתְּ? פּוּק, דְּלָאו אֹרַח אַרְעָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Objects to רב כהנא's presence, which was revealed in step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב כהנא's hiding under the bed
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Being present at such a private moment is a breach of דרך ארץ.

steps.title: רב כהנא answers: it is תורה
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא gives the same answer: it is Torah, and I need to learn.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: It is Torah, and I need to learn.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא repeats the familiar answer. Even the conduct of marital life is Torah that must be learned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase now completes three stories. Each story pushes the principle into a more private area. No area of life falls outside of Torah learning.
steps.whatToRemember: Three stories, one refrain: 'תורה היא וללמוד אני צריך'. Every part of a חכם's private conduct is Torah worth learning.

phrases.english: He said to him: It is Torah,
and I need to learn.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב's objection.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefinition of the value at stake
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Marital privacy is off-limits even for learning.
steps.terutzMaskana: This too is Torah that must be learned.

steps.title: Why wipe with the left and not the right?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks the reason for the third practice: why not wipe with the right hand?
steps.simpleTranslation: Why does one not wipe with the right hand, but with the left?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the third rule from the ברייתא and asks for its reason. This sets up a list of answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gave the practice without a reason. The question asks what makes the right hand special enough that it should not be used for this.

phrases.english: Why does one not wipe with the right hand
but with the left?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִפְּנֵי מָה אֵין מְקַנְּחִין בְּיָמִין אֶלָּא בִּשְׂמֹאל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the third rule from step 1 to explain its reason.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason the right hand is not used for wiping.

steps.title: רבא: the תורה was given with the right hand
steps.stepSummary: רבא: because the Torah was given with the right hand, as the פסוק says, 'מימינו אש דת למו'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Because the תורה was given with the right hand, as it is said: 'From His right hand, a fiery law for them.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives the first reason, which is based on a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the תורה came from השם's 'right hand', the right hand gains a special honor. So it should not be used for something degrading.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Because the Torah was given with the right hand,
as it is said: 'From His right hand, a fiery law for them.'
phrases.notes: דברים 33:2

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהַתּוֹרָה נִיתְּנָה בְּיָמִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: First answer to the question in step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The right hand is honored because the Torah was given with the right.

steps.title: רבה בר בר חנה: the right hand is close to the mouth
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה: because the right hand is close to the mouth, since one eats with it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said: Because it is close to the mouth.
steps.whatsHappening: A second reason is given, this one practical rather than based on a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: People eat with the right hand, so it should not be soiled. This reason is about cleanliness and practical use, not symbolism.

phrases.english: Rabbah bar bar Chana said:
Because it is close to the mouth.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהִיא קְרוֹבָה לַפֶּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: An alternative answer to step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: One eats with the right hand.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: one ties תפילין with the right hand
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן לקיש: because one ties תפילין with the right hand.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן לקיש said: Because one ties תפילין with it.
steps.whatsHappening: A third reason is given: the right hand is used for a מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תפילין are placed on the left arm and tied with the right hand. A hand used to perform a holy מצוה deserves respect.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said:
Because one ties tefillin with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ אָמַר: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁקּוֹשֵׁר בָּהּ תְּפִילִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third alternative answer to step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The right hand ties the תפילין.

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יצחק: one points to the תורה's notes with the right hand
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק: because one points out the טעמי תורה (cantillation) with the right hand.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: Because one shows the notes of the תורה with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The fourth and final reason: the right hand is used in teaching Torah.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Teachers and readers used hand motions to show the טעמים. A hand used to teach Torah should not be used for something lowly. All four answers agree that the right hand has special honor; they differ only on its source.
steps.whatToRemember: One wipes with the left hand. The right hand is honored for four suggested reasons: the Torah was given with the right (רבא), one eats with it (רבה בר בר חנה), one ties תפילין with it (ריש לקיש), and one shows the טעמים with it (רב נחמן בר יצחק).

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
Because one shows the notes of the Torah with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק אָמַר: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁמַּרְאֶה בָּהּ טַעֲמֵי תוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The fourth alternative answer to step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The right hand is used to show the טעמי תורה.

steps.title: The same reasons appear in a dispute among the תנאים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that the reasons for not wiping with the right hand match a dispute among תנאים: רבי אליעזר says it is because one eats with it, רבי יהושע says because one writes with it, and רבי עקיבא says because one points out the טעמי תורה with it.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like a dispute of the תנאים. רבי אליעזר says: because one eats with it. רבי יהושע says: because one writes with it. רבי עקיבא says: because one points out the cantillation notes of the תורה with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the different reasons the אמוראים gave in steps 11 to 14 were already argued about by earlier Sages, the תנאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר's reason (eating) matches רבה בר בר חנה, and רבי עקיבא's reason (טעמי תורה) matches רב נחמן בר יצחק. רבי יהושע adds a new reason, writing, which none of the אמוראים gave. The point is that this is an old dispute, and the אמוראים are following earlier opinions.

keyTerms.meaning: It is like a dispute of the תנאים (the Sages of the משנה era)
The cantillation notes of the Torah reading

steps.whatToRemember: There are many reasons the right hand is treated with honor: Torah was given with it, eating, writing, tying תפילין, and pointing out טעמי תורה. The תנאים already disagreed about which reason is the main one.

phrases.english: This is like a dispute among the Tannaim.
phrases.notes: It links the אמוראים' reasons above to an earlier dispute.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁאוֹכֵל בָּהּ.
phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says: Because he eats with it.
phrases.notes: This is the same reason רבה בר בר חנה gave (step 12).

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁכּוֹתֵב בָּהּ.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua says: Because he writes with it.
phrases.notes: A new reason not mentioned by the אמוראים.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says:
Because he points out the notes of the Torah with it.
phrases.notes: This is the same reason רב נחמן בר יצחק gave (step 14).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Places the reasons from steps 11 to 14 inside an older Tannaitic dispute.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The reason for not wiping with the right hand is disputed among the תנאים: eating, writing, or pointing out טעמי תורה.

steps.title: Modesty in the bathroom protects from three dangers
steps.stepSummary: רבי תנחום בר חנילאי teaches that whoever is modest in the בית הכסא is saved from snakes, scorpions, and מזיקין. Some say his dreams will also be calm.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי תנחום בר חנילאי said: Anyone who is modest in the bathroom is saved from three things: snakes, scorpions, and harmful spirits. Some say his dreams will also be calm for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new teaching about the reward for being modest in the בית הכסא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the topic was proper conduct in the בית הכסא. This מימרא adds that such conduct brings protection. The יש אומרים adds one more benefit: peaceful dreams.
steps.whyThisMatters: This teaching sets up the story that follows, which shows modesty protecting people from מזיקין.

phrases.english: Rabbi Tanḥum bar Ḥanilai said:
Anyone who is modest in the bathroom
is saved from three things:

phrases.aramaic: מִן הַנְּחָשִׁים, וּמִן הָעַקְרַבִּים, וּמִן הַמַּזִּיקִין.
phrases.english: from snakes, from scorpions, and from demons.
And some say
that even his dreams will be settled for him.
phrases.notes: His dreams will be calm and not disturbing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the right-hand discussion to a new teaching about modesty in the בית הכסא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Modesty in the בית הכסא protects from snakes, scorpions, and מזיקין, and according to some it also brings calm dreams.

steps.title: The dangerous bathroom in טבריא
steps.stepSummary: There was a בית הכסא in טבריא where people who entered two at a time were harmed, even during the day. רבי אמי and רבי אסי each entered alone and were not harmed.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a certain bathroom in טבריא. When two people went in together, they were harmed even in the daytime. רבי אמי and רבי אסי would each go in alone, and they were not harmed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story that shows the teaching of רבי תנחום in real life. It is setting up the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Going in two at a time was normally a way to stay safe, yet here it did not help. רבי אמי and רבי אסי went in alone, which looked more dangerous, but they were unharmed. This puzzle leads to the question that follows.

phrases.english: There was a certain bathroom in Tiberias,

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הֲווֹ עָיְילִי בֵּיהּ בֵּי תְרֵי —
phrases.english: when people would enter it two at a time,
even in the daytime they would be harmed.
phrases.notes: Normally daytime and company were thought to be safer.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ami and Rabbi Asi

phrases.aramaic: הֲווֹ עָיְילִי בֵּיהּ חַד וְחַד לְחוֹדֵיהּ —
phrases.english: would enter it, each one alone,
and they were not harmed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a story that illustrates the protection described in step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the dangerous bathroom of טבריא, pairs were harmed, but רבי אמי and רבי אסי entered alone and were safe.

steps.title: The Sages ask: aren't you afraid?
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן ask רבי אמי and רבי אסי whether they are afraid to enter that dangerous place alone.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages said to them: Aren't you afraid?
steps.whatsHappening: The other Sages ask a short question. It sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question points to the surprise in the story: everyone else was harmed, so why did these two feel safe going in alone? The answer will explain their secret.

phrases.english: The Sages said to them:
Aren't you afraid?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the surprising behavior described in step 17.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why are רבי אמי and רבי אסי not afraid to enter the dangerous bathroom alone?

steps.title: Their tradition: modesty and silence
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי and רבי אסי answer that they received a קבלה: in the בית הכסא, be modest and silent. For suffering, be silent and pray for mercy.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to them: We learned a tradition. The tradition for the bathroom is modesty and silence. The tradition for suffering is silence and asking for mercy.
steps.whatsHappening: The two Sages explain that a received tradition protects them: modest and quiet behavior in the בית הכסא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This confirms רבי תנחום's teaching from step 16, since modesty protects from מזיקין. They add silence as part of the protection. They also share a second tradition: when suffering comes, accept it quietly and pray.
steps.whatToRemember: In the בית הכסא, modesty and silence protect a person. In times of suffering, a person should stay silent and pray.

phrases.english: They said to them:
We have learned a tradition:
the tradition for the bathroom is
modesty and silence.
The tradition for suffering is
silence and asking for mercy.
phrases.notes: Accept it quietly without complaint, and pray.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They have a tradition that modesty and silence in the בית הכסא give protection, and that silence and prayer help in times of suffering.

steps.title: אביי's mother raised a lamb to accompany him
steps.stepSummary: אביי's mother raised a lamb so it could go with him into the בית הכסא, as protection from מזיקין.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי's mother raised a lamb for him to go in with him to the bathroom.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives another short story about protection from מזיקין in the בית הכסא. It sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since a person should not go in alone, having an animal along served as company and protection. The specific choice of a lamb will now be questioned.
steps.confusionAlert: אביי's birth mother died when he was born. The 'mother' here is the woman who raised him, whom he called 'mother'.

phrases.english: Abaye's mother raised a lamb for him
to enter the bathroom with him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another story about guarding against מזיקין in the בית הכסא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An animal was brought along into the בית הכסא as protection, and אביי's mother chose a lamb.

steps.title: Why not raise a goat instead?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: she should have raised a young goat for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: But she should have raised a young goat for him!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the choice of a lamb and suggests a goat would have been better.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumes a goat would have served at least as well as a lamb. So why did she choose a lamb? The next step explains the hidden reason.

phrases.english: But let her raise a goat for him!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the choice of a lamb in step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: The choice of a lamb as the animal companion.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A goat would seem to be an equally good or better choice, so why a lamb?

steps.title: A goat could be confused with a goat-demon
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers: a שעיר (goat) could be mixed up with a שעיר (goat-demon), so a lamb was safer.
steps.simpleTranslation: A goat could be mistaken for a goat-demon.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why a goat was avoided: it could be confused with a demon.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word שעיר means both 'goat' and a kind of demon (as in the פסוק 'ושעירים ירקדו שם'). In a place full of מזיקין, a goat could be mistaken for a demon, or a demon could disguise itself as the goat. A lamb avoids that confusion.

keyTerms.meaning: A goat, and also a goat-like demon

steps.whatToRemember: A lamb, not a goat, was chosen because the word שעיר can mean both a goat and a demon, so they could be confused.

phrases.english: A goat could be interchanged with a goat-demon.
phrases.notes: The same word, שעיר, means both a goat and a demon.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a hidden reason that explains the original choice.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A goat would be just as good as a lamb.
steps.terutzMaskana: A goat could be confused with a שעיר demon, so a lamb was chosen.

steps.title: How רבא's wife protected him in the bathroom
steps.stepSummary: Before רבא became ראש ישיבה, his wife (the daughter of רב חסדא) rattled a nut in a copper vessel to protect him. After he became leader, she made a window for him and placed her hand on his head.
steps.simpleTranslation: Before רבא became the head of the ישיבה, the daughter of רב חסדא would rattle a nut in a copper bowl for him. After he became the leader, she made a window for him and put her hand on his head.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells one more story about protecting a person from מזיקין in the בית הכסא, continuing the story of אביי's mother. Here רבא's wife does the protecting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rattling noise was meant to scare away מזיקין. Once רבא became a leader, he needed stronger protection, because important people are in greater danger from מזיקין. So his wife made a window, likely so she could reach him, and placed her hand on his head.

keyTerms.meaning: He reigned, meaning he became leader

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the danger from מזיקין was thought to grow with a person's importance. The greater the person, the more protection he needed.

phrases.english: Rava, before he became the head (of the yeshiva),
the daughter of Rav Chisda (his wife) would rattle for him
a nut in a copper vessel.
phrases.notes: The noise scared away מזיקין.

phrases.english: After he became leader,
she made a window for him,
and placed her hand on his head.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel story to אביי's mother raising a lamb. Another woman protects a great sage from מזיקין.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A leader needs greater protection from מזיקין than an ordinary person, so רבא's wife upgraded her method once he became ראש ישיבה.

steps.title: עולא: how far to go for privacy
steps.stepSummary: עולא rules that behind a fence a person may relieve himself right away. In an open valley he must go far enough that if he passes wind, nobody hears.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: Behind a fence, a person may relieve himself immediately. In a valley, he must go far enough that if he passes wind, his friend does not hear.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new practical topic: how far away a person must go to relieve himself privately. עולא gives two rules, one for behind a fence and one for an open field.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A fence already blocks people from seeing him, so according to עולא no extra distance is needed. In an open valley nothing hides him, so he must go far enough that people cannot even hear him.

keyTerms.meaning: Passes wind (literally: sneezes, used here as a polite word)

phrases.english: Ulla said:
Behind a fence, one may relieve himself immediately.
And in a valley,

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל זְמַן שֶׁמִּתְעַטֵּשׁ וְאֵין חֲבֵרוֹ שׁוֹמֵעַ.
phrases.english: (he must go) far enough that if he passes wind, his friend does not hear.

steps.confusionAlert: Here מתעטש does not mean sneezing. It is a polite way of saying passing wind.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from stories about מזיקין to a new halachic question of privacy distance.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Behind a fence, no distance is needed. In a valley, one must be out of hearing range.

steps.title: איסי בר נתן: a stricter version
steps.stepSummary: איסי בר נתן teaches that behind a fence one must be out of hearing range. In a valley one must be out of sight.
steps.simpleTranslation: איסי בר נתן taught it this way: Behind a fence, a person must go far enough that if he passes wind, his friend does not hear. In a valley, he must go far enough that his friend cannot see him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different version of the rule from איסי בר נתן. He is stricter in both places.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Behind a fence, עולא needed no distance at all, but איסי בר נתן requires going out of hearing range. In a valley, עולא required hearing distance, but איסי בר נתן requires going completely out of sight, which is much farther.

keyTerms.meaning: Teaches it this way (a different version)

steps.whyThisMatters: This stricter view, that even behind a fence some distance is needed, is the one the next step will challenge.

phrases.english: Isi bar Natan teaches it like this:
Behind a fence, (he must go) far enough that if he passes wind
his friend does not hear,

phrases.aramaic: וּבַבִּקְעָה — כׇּל זְמַן שֶׁאֵין חֲבֵרוֹ רוֹאֵהוּ.
phrases.english: and in a valley, far enough that his friend does not see him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a stricter alternative version of עולא's rule, raising each requirement one level.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Behind a fence, one must be out of hearing range. In a valley, one must be out of sight.

steps.title: Challenge from the workers at the olive press
steps.stepSummary: A משנה in טהרות says workers leave the olive press, relieve themselves right behind the fence, and stay pure. This suggests no distance is needed behind a fence, against איסי בר נתן.
steps.simpleTranslation: The גמרא objects: We learned that workers go out of the entrance of the olive press, relieve themselves behind the fence, and they are still pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges איסי בר נתן's strict rule using a משנה about olive-press workers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה pictures workers stepping just behind the fence of the olive press to relieve themselves. They do not go out of hearing range. This seems to show that behind a fence no distance is needed, which fits עולא and contradicts איסי בר נתן.

phrases.english: They objected:
They go out of the entrance of the olive press,
and relieve themselves behind the fence,
and they are pure!

steps.confusionAlert: The proof is not about purity itself. The point is that the משנה shows people relieving themselves right behind a fence, with no extra distance.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks איסי בר נתן's view from step 25.
steps.kashyaTarget: איסי בר נתן's rule that behind a fence one must go out of hearing range.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה describes workers relieving themselves immediately behind a fence, implying no extra distance is required.

steps.title: Purity laws are a special leniency
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that in matters of טהרות, חכמים were lenient. So the משנה does not prove the general rule about distance.
steps.simpleTranslation: Regarding purity, they were lenient.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends איסי בר נתן by saying the olive-press case is a special leniency connected to purity.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To help the workers stay pure, חכמים let them relieve themselves close by instead of going far away, where they might come into contact with impurity. This is an exception made for the sake of purity. Normally, איסי בר נתן's distance still applies.
steps.whatToRemember: עולא and איסי בר נתן argue about the required privacy distance. The משנה about olive-press workers does not disprove איסי בר נתן, because purity cases got a special leniency.

phrases.english: With regard to purity, they were lenient.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the קשיא from step 26 by limiting the משנה to a special case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the source to a special exception
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה proves that, in general, no distance is needed behind a fence.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה reflects a special leniency to protect purity. The general rule of איסי בר נתן still stands.

steps.title: A second purity source seems to clash with איסי בר נתן
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says workers need to go only so far that they can still be seen. This seems to contradict איסי בר נתן, who said that in a valley one must be out of sight.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: How far may they go away and still stay pure? Only so far that the other person can still see him!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another source to challenge איסי בר נתן. This one says the workers may stay within sight of each other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: איסי בר נתן said that in an open valley you must go far enough not to be seen. This ברייתא says the opposite: the worker stays where his friend can still see him. That way the friend can watch that he does not touch anything impure. So it looks like being out of sight is not required.

phrases.english: Come and hear: How far may they go away
and still remain pure?
Only so far that the other can still see him!
phrases.notes: This is the opposite of איסי בר נתן's 'out of sight' rule for a valley.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: כַּמָּה יַרְחִקוּ וְיִהְיוּ טְהוֹרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second challenge against איסי בר נתן, again taken from the laws of טהרות.
steps.kashyaTarget: איסי בר נתן's rule that in a valley one must be out of sight
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא allows the worker to stay within sight, so being out of sight does not seem to be required.

steps.title: People who eat in purity are a special case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that people eating in purity are different, because חכמים were lenient with them.
steps.simpleTranslation: People who eat their food in purity are different, because the Rabbis were lenient with them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the same answer it gave before. This purity case is a special leniency, so it does not teach the normal rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To protect the purity of the food, חכמים let these workers stay close by and in sight. That is an exception made for the sake of טהרות. The normal privacy rule of איסי בר נתן still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Those who eat their food in ritual purity

steps.confusionAlert: This is the same answer as step 27, but here it answers a new challenge. The גמרא really repeats it. It is not a copying mistake.

phrases.english: Those who eat in purity are different,
because the Rabbis were lenient with them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 28.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the source to a special case (an exception)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא shows that being in sight is fine for everyone.
steps.terutzMaskana: The leniency applies only to people eating in purity. The general rule is unchanged.

steps.title: רב אשי explains what איסי בר נתן meant by 'not seen'
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי explains that איסי בר נתן only required that one's uncovered body not be seen. The friend may still see the person himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: What does 'as long as his friend does not see him' mean, which איסי בר נתן said? It means as long as his friend does not see his uncovered body. But the friend may see the person himself.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives a different way to remove the contradiction. He reads איסי בר נתן's words more narrowly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is no need for a special purity leniency. איסי בר נתן never said the person himself must be out of sight, only his uncovered body. So the ברייתא ('the friend sees him') and איסי בר נתן agree.
steps.whatToRemember: Two answers to the challenge: (1) a special leniency for טהרות; (2) רב אשי: 'out of sight' means only that the uncovered body is not seen.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
What does 'as long as his friend does not see' mean,
which Isi bar Natan said?

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל זְמַן שֶׁאֵין חֲבֵרוֹ רוֹאֶה אֶת פֵּרוּעוֹ,
phrases.english: As long as his friend does not see his uncovered body,
but the friend may see him himself.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: מַאי כׇּל זְמַן שֶׁאֵין חֲבֵרוֹ רוֹאֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to the challenge of step 28 by reinterpreting איסי בר נתן.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the meaning of a word or phrase
steps.terutzHavaAmina: איסי בר נתן meant that the whole person must be out of sight.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the uncovered body must be out of sight, so there is no contradiction.

steps.title: A eulogizer praises a dead man as modest
steps.stepSummary: A eulogizer spoke in front of רב נחמן and said the dead man was modest in his ways.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain eulogizer went down to speak in front of רב נחמן. He said: 'This man was modest in his ways.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a short story connected to modesty in the bathroom. This line sets up רב נחמן's reaction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The eulogizer gives the dead man general praise for being a צנוע. The story will test what that praise really means.

keyTerms.meaning: A eulogizer (someone who gives the funeral speech)

phrases.english: There was a certain eulogizer
who went down to speak before Rav Nachman,
He said: 'This man was modest in his ways.'

steps.triggerLanguage: הַהוּא סַפְדָנָא דִּנְחֵית קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from distance rules to a story about the meaning of modesty in the בית הכסא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The eulogizer calls the dead man צנוע.

steps.title: רב נחמן asks how the eulogizer could know
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן challenges the eulogizer: did you go into the bathroom with him? A ברייתא says that true modesty is measured in the בית הכסא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said to him: Did you go into the bathroom with him, so that you know if he was modest or not? For a ברייתא teaches: we only call someone 'modest' if he is modest in the bathroom.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן challenges the praise. He backs up his challenge with a ברייתא about what 'modest' really means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to the ברייתא, real צניעות is how a person behaves when nobody sees him, like in the bathroom. The eulogizer could not know that. So his praise was not based on knowledge.
steps.whyThisMatters: This defines צניעות as private behavior, not public image. It also ties the story back to the sugya's topic of conduct in the bathroom.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said to him:
Did you go with him into the bathroom
so that you know whether he was modest or not?
As it was taught: We do not call someone 'modest'
except one who is modest in the bathroom.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב נַחְמָן: אַתְּ עֲיַילְתְּ בַּהֲדֵיהּ לְבֵית הַכִּסֵּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the eulogizer's praise from step 31.
steps.kashyaTarget: The eulogizer's claim that the dead man was צנוע
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Modesty is judged by private behavior in the bathroom, which the eulogizer could not have seen.

steps.title: Why did רב נחמן care so much?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what difference it made to רב נחמן whether the praise was exact.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what difference did it make to רב נחמן?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רב נחמן objected at all to some kind words at a funeral. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Praising the dead seems harmless, even if it is a bit exaggerated. The גמרא wants to know what real problem רב נחמן saw.

keyTerms.meaning: What difference does it make to him?

phrases.english: And Rav Nachman,
what difference did it make to him?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב נַחְמָן מַאי נָפְקָא לֵיהּ מִינֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind רב נחמן's objection in step 32.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רב נחמן insisted that the praise be accurate

steps.title: Eulogizers are punished for false praise
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that just as the dead are punished, so are the eulogizers and those who answer after them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because a ברייתא teaches: Just as the dead are punished, so too the eulogizers are punished, and also those who answer after them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that false praise brings punishment on the speaker and on those who agree. That is why רב נחמן spoke up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Giving the dead person praise he did not earn is a lie, and the eulogizer is held responsible for it. Even the people who answer after him share the blame, because they agree to it. רב נחמן was protecting the eulogizer and the audience.

keyTerms.meaning: Those who answer after them (the people who agree)

steps.whatToRemember: Real צניעות is shown in private. A eulogy must be truthful, because false praise is punished, even for those who agree with it.

phrases.english: Because it was taught:
Just as the dead are punished,
so too the eulogizers are punished,
and those who answer after them.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשּׁוּם דְּתַנְיָא: כְּשֵׁם שֶׁנִּפְרָעִין מִן הַמֵּתִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 33.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: False praise in a eulogy brings punishment on the eulogizer and on those who answer after him, so רב נחמן had to object.

steps.title: A ברייתא defines who is truly modest
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that a צנוע is one who relieves himself at night in the same place he would by day.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: Who is a modest person? One who relieves himself at night in the same place where he relieves himself during the day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא that gives a test for real modesty: someone who acts the same in the dark as in daylight.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At night nobody can see, so a person might be tempted to relieve himself close by. The ברייתא says a truly modest person still goes as far as he would by day. This sets up the challenge that comes next.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
Who is a modest person?
This is one who relieves himself at night
in the place where he relieves himself during the day.
phrases.notes: In other words, he goes just as far away at night as he does by day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of modesty in the בית הכסא raised in רב נחמן's challenge to the eulogizer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A modest person relieves himself at night in the same place, and at the same distance, as he does by day.

steps.title: רב taught that a person should train himself so he will not need to go far
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא using רב's teaching that one should relieve himself in the dark of morning and evening so he will not have to go far.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that so? But didn't רב יהודה say in the name of רב: A person should always train himself to relieve himself early in the morning and late in the evening, so that he will not need to go far away!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the ברייתא by quoting רב, who seems to say that at night you do NOT need to go far.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב's advice is to go when it is dark precisely so that you can stay nearby. That suggests the night rules are more relaxed than the day rules. This contradicts the ברייתא, which says to go to the same place at night as by day.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Is that so?!' It signals a challenge
A person should always accustom himself
Early morning and evening, when it is still dark
To distance himself, i.e., go far away

phrases.english: Is that so?!
But didn't Rav Yehuda say in the name of Rav:
A person should always accustom himself
to relieve himself in the morning and in the evening,
so that he will not need to go far away!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִינִי?! וְהָאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ברייתא in step 35.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's rule that at night one goes to the same place as by day
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב says that darkness lets a person avoid going far, so at night one need not go as far as by day.

steps.title: רבא and רבי זירא went close by at night
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא adds a further challenge from the practice of רבא, who went a מיל away by day but nearby at night, and of רבי זירא, who went behind the study hall.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore: by day רבא would go as far as a מיל, but at night he would tell his attendant, 'Clear me a spot in the town street.' Similarly, רבי זירא told his attendant, 'See who is behind the study hall, because I need to relieve myself!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא strengthens its challenge with stories of great אמוראים who did not go far at night.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא clearly treated day and night differently: far by day, close by at night. רבי זירא also went right behind the study hall. Their real-life practice contradicts the ברייתא's demand to use the same place at night.

keyTerms.meaning: And furthermore; it adds another challenge
The study hall, the house of the scholars

phrases.english: And furthermore, Rava, during the day,
would go as far as a mil,
but at night he would say to his attendant:
Clear a place for me in the town street.

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן אָמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי זֵירָא לְשַׁמָּעֵיהּ:
phrases.english: And similarly, Rabbi Zeira said to his attendant:
See who is there
behind the study hall,
because I need to relieve myself!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתוּ, רָבָא בִּימָמָא הֲוָה אָזֵיל עַד מִיל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second, practical challenge on top of רב's teaching against the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's rule of using the same place at night as by day
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Leading אמוראים relieved themselves much closer at night than by day, so day and night are treated differently.

steps.title: Change the wording to 'in the same manner'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers by changing the ברייתא's wording: not 'in the place' but 'in the manner' one relieves himself by day.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do not say 'in the place.' Rather, say: 'in the manner in which he relieves himself during the day.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenges by fixing the wording of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא is not about distance at all. It is about behavior: at night a person should uncover himself just as modestly as he would by day. That way, staying close by at night (as רב advised, and as רבא and רבי זירא did) is fine, as long as he stays just as modest.

keyTerms.meaning: Don't say this, rather say that; it emends a text

steps.confusionAlert: The new version does NOT require going far at night. 'כדרך' refers to how modestly he behaves, not where he goes.

phrases.english: Do not say 'in the place,'
rather say:
in the manner in which he relieves himself during the day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenges of steps 36 and 37.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא required going the same distance at night as by day.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא only requires the same modest behavior at night as by day. Distance does not matter.

steps.title: רב אשי keeps the wording and applies it to a corner
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says that even keeping 'in the place,' the ברייתא refers only to stepping behind a corner, not to going far away.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Even if you keep the wording 'in the place,' it is needed only for the case of a corner.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives a different answer that leaves the ברייתא's original words in place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By day a person ducks behind a nearby corner to hide himself. The ברייתא means that at night he should still go behind that corner and not relieve himself out in the open. That is a short distance, so it does not clash with רב, רבא or רבי זירא.

keyTerms.meaning: Even if you say; it keeps the original reading

steps.whatToRemember: There are two answers. Either the ברייתא is about manner, not place, or it is about a nearby corner, not a far distance. Either way, one need not go far at night, but one must stay modest.

phrases.aramaic: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא בַּמָּקוֹם,
phrases.english: Rav Ashi said: Even if you say 'in the place,'
it was needed only for a corner.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא בַּמָּקוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers an alternative answer to step 38 without changing the text.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (אוקימתא) while keeping the original wording
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'In the place' meant going the same far distance at night.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'In the place' means the same hidden corner. At night he should still hide behind it.

steps.title: Opening a discussion of רב's teaching on its own
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא re-quotes רב's statement about training oneself to go in the morning and evening, in order to discuss it directly.
steps.simpleTranslation: The matter itself: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: A person should always train himself to relieve himself in the morning and in the evening, so that he will not need to go far away.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It brings back רב's teaching, quoted earlier only as a challenge, so it can now analyze that teaching itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, רב's words served only as a tool to attack the ברייתא. With 'גופא' the גמרא turns the spotlight onto the teaching itself, and a discussion of it will follow.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The matter itself': the גמרא returns to examine a statement quoted earlier
רב יהודה quoting his teacher רב, a common chain of tradition

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new challenge. It is the same statement as in step 36, now quoted for discussion in its own right.

phrases.english: The matter itself.
Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav:
A person should always accustom himself
to relieve himself in the morning and in the evening,
so that he will not need to go far away.

steps.triggerLanguage: גּוּפָא. אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the statement cited in step 36 in order to examine it directly.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person should train himself to relieve himself in the dark of early morning and evening so that he need not go far away.

steps.title: A ברייתא from בן עזאי supports רב's advice
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא in which בן עזאי says to go out early in the morning and in the evening so you will not have to go far. This matches רב's statement.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught this way in a ברייתא: בן עזאי says: Get up early and go out, wait for evening and go out, so that you will not need to go far away.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says the same thing as רב, to show that רב's advice has an earlier source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב said to train yourself to relieve yourself in the dark of morning and evening so you won't have to go far. בן עזאי says the same thing in nearly the same words: go out early or late, 'so that you will not distance yourself.' The reason matches too: in the dark there is privacy nearby, so walking far for modesty is unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way (introduces a ברייתא that supports what was just said)
Wait until evening and go out
So that you will not have to go far

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that רב's practical advice is rooted in a תנאי source, which strengthens it after the earlier challenges about how far one must go for modesty.

phrases.english: It was also taught this way:
phrases.notes: This is how the גמרא brings a ברייתא that backs up what was just said.

phrases.english: Ben Azzai says:
Rise early and go out,
phrases.notes: Go to relieve yourself before daybreak.

phrases.english: wait for evening and go out,
phrases.notes: Go after dark.

phrases.english: so that you will not need to go far.
phrases.notes: Same reason רב gave.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב's statement, which was re-quoted in step 40.
steps.raayaObject: רב's teaching to relieve oneself in the morning and evening dark so as not to go far.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא quoting בן עזאי: 'השכם וצא, הערב וצא, כדי שלא תתרחק.'

steps.title: Prepare first and then sit, not the other way around
steps.stepSummary: בן עזאי adds that a person should touch (to help the body open) before sitting, not sit and then touch, because sitting first leaves him open to כשפים done even far away.
steps.simpleTranslation: Touch first and then sit; do not sit and then touch. Anyone who sits and then touches, even if כשפים are done far away in אספמיא, they come upon him.
steps.whatsHappening: The same ברייתא of בן עזאי continues with a new piece of practical advice: the right order is to prepare first and then sit down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a new teaching, not the support for רב. The order matters: touching first and then sitting is correct, while sitting first and then touching is harmful. The danger is spiritual: such a person becomes open to כשפים, even sorcery done in a far-off place like אספמיא (Spain).

keyTerms.meaning: Touches (here: touching around the opening to help the body release)
Spain, a symbol of a very distant place
They come upon him (they affect him)

steps.confusionAlert: This is still the same ברייתא of בן עזאי, but it is a separate teaching. It is not part of the proof for רב.

phrases.english: Touch and then sit,
phrases.notes: Prepare first, then sit down.

phrases.english: and do not sit and then touch,
for anyone who sits and then touches,
even if sorcery is performed in Aspamia,
phrases.notes: Even from very far away.

phrases.english: it comes upon him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא of בן עזאי with a new instruction about the order of sitting and touching.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Touch first and then sit. Sitting first and then touching exposes a person to כשפים, even from far away.

steps.title: What if someone forgot and sat first?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what remedy there is for a person who forgot and sat down first, then touched.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if he forgot and sat, and only afterward touched, what is his remedy?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a practical follow-up question about someone who already made the mistake בן עזאי warned against. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בן עזאי described a danger but gave no fix. The גמרא now asks whether anything can be done once the mistake has already happened.

phrases.english: And if he forgot and sat
and afterward touched,
what is his remedy?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי אִנְּשִׁי וִיתִיב וְאַחַר כָּךְ מַשְׁמֵשׁ, מַאי תַּקַּנְתֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for a remedy for someone who broke the rule in step 42.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What can a person do to protect himself if he sat before touching?

steps.title: A protective formula to say when standing up
steps.stepSummary: When he stands up, he should say a formula rejecting all kinds of כשפים: 'Not for me, not for me,' naming the types of sorcery and the sorcerers.
steps.simpleTranslation: When he stands, let him say this: 'Not for me, not for me; neither תחים nor תחתים; neither these nor anything from these; neither the sorcery of a sorcerer nor the sorcery of a sorceress.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question: the person should say a short protective statement when he gets up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fix is verbal. The person declares that no kind of sorcery should take hold of him. The formula names specific types (תחים and תחתים), everything connected to them, and sorcery from both a man and a woman, so it rejects every possible source.

keyTerms.meaning: Not for me (may it not affect me)

steps.whatToRemember: בן עזאי's ברייתא backs רב: go early or late so you don't need to go far. It also teaches to prepare before sitting, and if one forgot, he says the protective formula 'לא לי לא לי' when he stands.

phrases.english: When he stands, let him say this:
"Not for me, not for me,
neither taḥim nor taḥtim,
phrases.notes: Types of sorcery.

phrases.english: neither these nor from these,
phrases.notes: Neither the spells themselves nor anything coming from them.

phrases.english: neither the sorcery of a sorcerer
nor the sorcery of a sorceress."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 43.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: When he stands, he says: 'לא לי לא לי, לא תחים ולא תחתים, לא הני ולא מהני, לא חרשי דחרשא ולא חרשי דחרשתא.'
